task.description: Write ExUnit tests (and any needed .wat fixtures) satisfying every REQ-173 acceptance criterion below, using the design's specified controllable-gate mechanism (a fake/test-double service caller that blocks on a synchronization primitive until released, reused from REQ-172's do_call_service/8 seam) to hold one invocation open while a concurrent activate/2 call installs a new module version, then assert BOTH halves in one overlapping scenario: the held invocation completes against the OLD version's behaviour and capability set, and a NEW invocation started after activation observes the NEW version's behaviour and capability set. Assert the prior version's resources are released only after its last in-flight invocation completes (not at activation time) -- check ModuleVersionRegistry's internal release/ref-count behavior via its own accessor functions, not by inference. Assert capability isolation explicitly: when the new version's manifest declares a DIFFERENT capability set than the old one, the held (old-version) invocation must still succeed/fail exactly as the old capability set would dictate, and the new invocation must be governed by the new capability set -- test both directions (old allows what new denies, and vice versa) if the design's fixtures support it. Apply this project's mutation-testing discipline: for each acceptance criterion, mutate the real implementation locally, confirm the pre-existing suite fails to catch it, add a closing test, then revert the mutation and verify the revert (git diff/md5sum) before finishing. Do not modify lib/letflow/engine/wasm/module_registry.ex, capability_gate.ex, or plugin_handler.ex. Run mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix test yourself, quote real output.
acceptance_criteria: a test holds an invocation open (a guest blocked in a controllable host call), activates a new module version DURING it, and asserts the held invocation completes normally against the OLD version's observable behaviour -- WASM-14's own acceptance criterion, with the overlap real rather than sequential
the same test asserts an invocation started AFTER the activation observes the NEW version's behaviour, so both halves of WASM-14 are proven in one overlapping scenario
the two module versions used are observably different in output, so the test can distinguish which version served an invocation rather than merely completing
a test asserts the prior version's resources are released only after its last in-flight invocation completes, not at activation time

a test asserts that when the new version's manifest declares a DIFFERENT capability set, an in-flight invocation of the prior version keeps the prior version's capability set, and the new invocation gets the new one -- so activation cannot silently widen or narrow a running invocation's authority
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
